Comparing against grieg.mp3 and generate_grieg_midi.py exposed the exact bug that caused the "weird drop key" in our Python synth:

float32 Phase Accumulation Precision Loss (np.cumsum):

In mountain_king_music.py (and norvid_computing.py), np.cumsum(mel_f) was accumulating frequency in 32-bit float (np.float32, which only has 24 mantissa bits).
Once np.cumsum(mel_f) passed ~1.34e8 around t = 8s, the float32 unit-in-last-place (ulp) grew to 16 Hz–32 Hz, rounding every note's frequency (369.99 Hz F#4, 329.63 Hz E4, etc.) to coarse multiples of 16 Hz and detuning the melody into a completely different key!
Switching phase accumulation to np.float64 (np.cumsum(mel_f.astype(np.float64))) completely eliminates the pitch drift.

Exact Grieg Score Notes (matching grieg.mp3 & generate_grieg_midi.py):

Bar 1: B3 – C#4 – D4 – E4 – F#4 – D4 – F#4
Bar 2: F4 (E#4) – C#4 – F4 (E#4) – E4 – C4 – E4
Bar 3: B3 – C#4 – D4 – E4 – F#4 – D4 – F#4 – B4
Bar 4: A4 – F#4 – D4 – F#4 – A4
